chunks: Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Al-Husayn ibn Saeed, from Fazalat ibn Ayoub, from Aban, from Muhammad Al-Halby, who said:

I asked Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him) about the ritual bath (ghusl) when one intends to pelt (the Jamarah). So he (peace be upon him) said: 'Sometimes I bathe. But, as for it being from the Sunnah, then no (it is not so).'

key_terms.يَرْمِيَ: He pelted (referring to throwing stones at the Jamarah)

ai.seo_question: Is ghusl before pelting the Jamarah a Sunnah or a ritual purity requirement?
ai.summary: In this narration from *Al-Kafi*, Imam al-Sadiq (AS) clarifies the status of *ghusl* before pelting the Jamarah during the days of Tashreeq, distinguishing between personal practice and obligatory or strongly recommended Sunnah. This ruling is significant for Hajj jurisprudence, as it prevents the innovation of treating this bath as a mandatory pillar, aligning with the Shia view that while recommended, it is not essential for the validity of the stoning ritual. The hadith underscores the principle of distinguishing between customary practices of the Imams and binding religious obligations.
